record.paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
record.context_brief: Bending laminations determine GHMC AdS structure
record.original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let M = S × R, and let l_- and l_+ be two measured laminations on S that fill S. Is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations exactly l_- and l_+?

evidence.quote: Question 3.1. If l− and l+ are two measured laminations which fill S, is there a unique GHMC AdS structure h on M such that l− and l+ are the measured bending laminations of the boundary of the convex core?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure on $M$ is a Lorentzian structure of constant sectional curvature $-1$ that admits a Cauchy surface diffeomorphic to $S$ and is maximal (with respect to isometric embedding) among such structures. Every GHMC AdS structure on $M$ contains a smallest non-empty geodesically convex closed subset, called the convex core, whose topological boundary (when the structure is not Fuchsian) consists of two pleated spacelike surfaces, each homeomorphic to $S$, bent along measured geodesic laminations $l_-$ and $l_+$ on $S$ called the lower and upper measured bending laminations.

Two measured geodesic laminations $l_-, l_+$ on $S$ are said to fill $S$ if for every essential simple closed curve $\gamma \subset S$ the sum of the geometric intersection numbers $i(\gamma, l_-) + i(\gamma, l_+)$ is positive.

Question: Given any two measured geodesic laminations $l_-$ and $l_+$ on $S$ that fill $S$, does there exist a unique GHMC AdS structure on $M$ whose convex-core boundary has $l_-$ and $l_+$ as its lower and upper measured bending laminations, respectively?
artifact.status_search_result: Existence has been established (by Tamburelli, and also Bonsante–Schlenker for related realization statements): for any pair of filling measured laminations there exists a GHMC AdS structure realizing them as bending laminations of the convex core. Uniqueness, however, remains open in general; rigidity has only been proved in special regimes such as small laminations near the Fuchsian locus, and a recent (2025) preprint addresses rigidity near the Fuchsian locus. Thus the full question remains partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Rigidity of anti-de Sitter (2+1)-spacetimes with convex boundary near the Fuchsian locus
status_evidence.snippet: For two measured laminations that fill S, there exists ǫ>0 such that for all t∈(0,ǫ), there exists a unique GHMC AdS manifold such that the measured bending laminations are tλ and tµ. ... The existence part was proved by Tamburelli; uniqueness remains elusive in general.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is known; uniqueness has been proved only near the Fuchsian locus.

status_evidence.title: Bending laminations on convex hulls of anti-de Sitter quasicircles
status_evidence.snippet: Any pair of bounded measured laminations that strongly fill can be obtained as bending laminations of the convex hull boundary in AdS^3.
status_evidence.claim: Realization (existence) of filling bending laminations is established in the related universal/quasicircle setting.
